name: Kemet and Kush: Spirituality
tag: Teaches Kemetic and Kushite creation stories and the story of Ausar, Aset and Heru.

scenarios.title: Teach the story of Ausar, Aset and Heru
scenarios.ask: Build a {length} lesson on Ausar, Aset and Heru for {students} {grade} students.
steps: Storyteller
Told the story in {=4 + grade} illustrated scenes, from Ausar's rule to Heru's claim to the throne.
Context
Explained the Greek names students may know: Osiris, Isis and Horus.
Discussion
Wrote questions on loyalty, grief and justice, and split the class into {=ceil(students / 5)} groups.
Quiz
Built a {=4 + grade * 2}-question check for understanding.
followups: Is there one official version of the story?
No. The story was told differently across periods and places. The app shows the main versions and notes which texts each comes from.
Is this suitable for younger students?
The middle school version leaves out the more violent details and focuses on Aset's search and Heru's growth.

scenarios.title: Compare creation stories
scenarios.ask: Compare {stories} creation stories, about {mins} on each.
steps: Library
Opened the Iunu (Heliopolis) account of Atum and the Ennead, the Khemenu (Hermopolis) Ogdoad of eight primeval beings, and the Memphite account of Ptah.
Kush link
Noted that the Shabaka Stone, which preserves the Memphite text, was carved under the Kushite king Shabaka.
Comparer
Lined up shared themes, such as the primeval waters of Nun and the first mound rising from them.
Visuals
Built a side-by-side chart of who creates, how, and what comes first in each of the {stories} stories.

result.title: Comparison ready
rows: Primeval waters and a first mound

followups: Why are there several creation stories?
Different temple centers developed their own accounts. The app presents them side by side rather than ranking them.
The app covers Kushite kings who ruled Egypt as the 25th Dynasty and the Amun temple at Jebel Barkal, and marks where sources are thin.

scenarios.title: Create an exhibit for a cultural event
scenarios.ask: We expect {visitors} visitors. Build a {panels}-panel exhibit on Kemet and Kush spirituality.
steps: Curator
Picked {panels} themes, from creation stories to the Ausar, Aset and Heru cycle.
Writer
Wrote about 120 words per panel in plain language, with sources on each.
Audio guide
Recorded a {=round(panels * 1.5)}-minute audio guide visitors can play on their phones.
Planner
Estimated visitor flow and screen needs.
followups: Yes. Each panel exports as a print-ready poster and as a slide.
The app cites a source on every panel. We suggest a local scholar or educator review before the event.
